query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a secondary phase to single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloys can overcome the coercivity limitation.
generation.conditions: Room temperature, no external magnetic field
generation.mechanism: Transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP) effect and lattice misfit
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased coercive field (Hc) without sacrificing saturation magnetization (Ms)
generation.baseline: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloy with Hc < 100 Oe
generation.boundary: Alloy composition, processing conditions, and measurement techniques
generation.uncertainty: Optimal secondary phase composition and volume fraction, effects of grain size and impurities

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare single-phase fcc FeCoNi and dual-phase FeCoNi alloys with varying secondary phase compositions and volume fractions. Measure the coercive field (Hc) and saturation magnetization (Ms) using standard magnetometry techniques.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the dual-phase alloys exhibit no significant increase in Hc (> 100 Oe) without sacrificing Ms, the hypothesis is falsified.
